name: ext_temp
source: 21 1A@8; external temperature sensor. The sensor is NOT present on the Td5 ECU (RDL016) → constant 0x1088 = 150.0 °C, a phantom reading. Confirmed in the car 2026-08-21: actual outside temp ~17 °C (the car's own cluster sensor via BCU), so 150 = false. Limits [-40,50] set so 150 is flagged suspect/struck-through. The value means nothing.

name: manifold_press
source: 21 1C@0 u16/10000 bar = TURBO/boost pressure (reference tool 'Turbo Pressure'). Idle ~1.0 bar (atmospheric); full load 2.0–2.2 bar absolute; the ECU's overboost cut is relative to ambient: ≈ +142 kPa above atmospheric (defender2 topic65863), i.e. ~2.42 bar at sea level. CONFIRMED 2026-08-03 (1.0→1.2 bar).
label: Turbo pressure
description: Turbo / boost pressure, absolute (bar). Idle ≈ ambient (~1.0); full load 2.0–2.2; overboost cut ≈ ambient + 1.42 bar.

label: RPM error
description: Idle-speed error: target minus actual idle rpm.

name: injection_qty
source: 21 1D@6 u16 x0.01 mg/stroke = INJECTION QUANTITY. PROVEN (field) via car test 2026-08-21 with deliberate overrun lifts: idle 11.1, load 23.9, OVERRUN 4.7 mg/stroke (falls below idle = fuel cut) = unambiguous fuelling signature. Gives a plausible live economy ~7.6 L/100km. Ekaitza calls 21 1D 'fuel-usage'. NOTE: the exact SCALE (x0.01) is matched against the SimonRafferty reference, not cross-checked against a factory tool on RDL016 — plausible but fine-tunable. Drives the trip computer (fuel_rate/economy, candidate).
label: Injection
description: Injection quantity (mg/stroke). Idle ~6–10; rises with load.

name: egr_modulator
source: 21 1D byte15 u8 x(100/255) = EGR Modulator % (duty). Confirmed across FOUR drives 2026-08-21/22: high at light load, falls to 0 under load/boost = textbook EGR (open light-load, closes under load). Idle duty varies by conditions (~13-62%). Identified via the Nanocom fuelling-page field order. NOTE: the adjacent 1D@16 (which the page order would put as 'EGR Inlet') reads a CONSTANT 0 across all four drives = a dead/reserved byte, so EGR Inlet is NOT @16 and is not yet located. Scale 100/255 is a candidate byte->% mapping, not cross-checked vs a factory tool. EGR was modulating (not stuck) - relevant to the intermittent 001-07.
label: EGR
description: EGR modulator duty % (1D@15, candidate).

name: wastegate_modulator
source: 21 1D byte17 u8 x(100/255) = Wastegate Modulator % (boost-control duty). Confirmed across four drives 2026-08-21/22: rises with boost (r=0.85 vs MAP) but is NOT MAP itself (1D@4 is MAP, r=0.995). Baseline ~15 raw (~6%), tops 25-82 raw (~10-32%) scaling with drive intensity - matches the published band (0% idle, 20-40% boost, max ~40%). Position matches the Nanocom fuelling-page order. Candidate scaling (100/255).
label: Wastegate
description: Wastegate modulator duty % (1D@17, candidate).

name: maf
source: 21 1D u16@4 (big-endian) = the ECU's air-mass value. FIELD proven (r=+0.95 vs rpm*MAP over a full WOT pull, raw log 2026-08-21). BUT this is almost certainly a MODELLED (speed-density) air mass, NOT the physical MAF sensor: RDL016 has 'air flow circuit (Current)' as a live fault and the MEASURED MAF (1C@4) reads 0 = dead sensor. The high rpm*MAP correlation is exactly what a modelled substitute looks like. So a plausible value here (idle ~53 kg/h) is NOT evidence the sensor is healthy - the dashboard shows a modelled value under a 'maf' name. scale/bias = provisional 2-point fit (idle ~60, 2000 rpm ~190 kg/h), never solid. T-01 in references/test_plan.md confirms 1C@4=measured on a healthy MAF and will then rename this field to a modelled air mass. COMPARISON 2026-10-04 with the live sensor (1C@4 x0.1): this calibrated value read 84/113/225 vs measured 48/114/215 kg/h at idle/1500/2600 rpm — agrees above idle, overstates idle. Consistent with a modelled air mass; the measured MAF is now maf_sensor.
label: Air flow
description: Air mass (1D u16@4) — likely a MODELLED value, not the sensor. RDL016's physical MAF (1C@4) reads 0 (air-flow-circuit fault), so this is the ECU's speed-density estimate. Candidate scale; see test T-01.

name: maf_sensor
source: 21 1C@4 = PHYSICAL MAF sensor (hot-film, 3-wire). Faulted on RDL016 (reads 0/stuck) — logged RAW to confirm whether it EVER responds to airflow, vs the 1D@4 MODELLED air mass. Separate upstream IAT feeds the model. 2026-08-29. UPDATE 2026-10-04: after the Td5 fault clear the sensor came alive. Stationary revs in P: idle 760rpm/1.04bar -> 478, 1575/1.09 -> 1143, 2600/1.29 -> 2154 (repeat 2119-2147): proportional to rpm x MAP (ratio 0.61/0.67/0.64). Scale x0.1 kg/h (BinOwl_Td5Gauge) gives 48/114/215 kg/h, physically plausible for 2.5 L (theoretical ~62/~260 at VE 0.9). Earlier zeros = sensor faulted. Field identity strong; scale from the reference + physics. Re-read through the decoder on the car 2026-10-04 after a dashboard restart: idle 47.5 kg/h (1.76 V), 2560 rpm 207-210 kg/h (3.41-3.43 V) vs modelled 213-218 -> proven (field identity; x0.1 scale per the reference + physics).
label: Air flow (measured)
description: Physical MAF sensor (1C@4), u16 x0.1 kg/h. Live once the 'air flow circuit' fault was cleared (2026-10-04).

name: wastegate_pos
source: 21 38@0 u16 (big-endian) = wastegate modulator %, the NATIVE-LID alternative to our 1D@17 duty candidate. Ported from SimonRafferty (TD5_PROTOCOL_REFERENCE.md) and his newer SimonRafferty/Td5-Diagnostic-App (td5_provider.cpp), both raw/100, the latter commenting explicitly 'not /1000'; BinOwl's /1000 is now the outlier. 0x38 responds on RDL016 (our 2026-08-08 idle capture: 04 61 38 00 00 = 0.0%). The Simon app places EGR/wastegate ONLY at native 0x37/0x38 (nothing in 1D), which conflicts with our 1D@17 candidate — resolver: test T-02.
label: Wastegate (0x38)
description: Wastegate modulator % from native LID 0x38 (candidate, /100 per two Simon sources). Native-vs-1D@17 conflict — see T-02.

name: egr_pos
source: 21 37@0 u16 (big-endian) = EGR modulator %, the NATIVE-LID alternative to our 1D@15 duty candidate. Ported from SimonRafferty (TD5_PROTOCOL_REFERENCE.md) and SimonRafferty/Td5-Diagnostic-App (td5_provider.cpp), both raw/100. 0x37 responds on RDL016 (our 2026-08-08 idle capture: 04 61 37 00 00 = 0.0%). The Simon app places EGR at native 0x37 (nothing in 1D), conflicting with our 1D@15 candidate — resolver: test T-02. (The EGR INLET is separately at 0x45, see egr_inlet.)
label: EGR (0x37)
description: EGR modulator % from native LID 0x37 (candidate, /100 per two Simon sources). Native-vs-1D@15 conflict — see T-02.

name: battery_direct
source: 21 10@2 u16/1000 V = a SECOND battery reading ('Battery Direct'). CORRECTION 2026-10-01: the older SimonRafferty .md called 0x10@2 'reference voltage', but the newer SimonRafferty/Td5-Diagnostic-App (td5_provider.cpp) decodes 0x10 as battery@0 + 'Battery Direct'@2 (both mV), and puts the 5V sensor reference in 0x1B (@8 NNN / @6 MSB = our accel_supply). So this is a battery reading, not a sensor ref. Was briefly stored as reference_voltage. Unverified on RDL016.
label: Battery (direct)
description: Second battery reading, 'Battery Direct' (0x10@2, candidate). The 5V sensor reference is accel_supply (1B@6), not here.

name: driver_demand
source: 21 1D@0 = driver's demand (pedal-derived request, vs injection_qty@6 = delivered). CONFLICT: BinOwl reads it as fuel demand mg/stroke (u16 x0.01); SimonRafferty/Td5-Diagnostic-App reads it as pedal position % (i16 /100). Stored as mg/stroke pending the car; either way it tracks the pedal and drops to ~0 on overrun. Resolver: test T-03.
label: Driver demand
description: Driver's demand (1D@0, candidate) — pedal request; mg/stroke (BinOwl) vs % (Simon app), drops to ~0 on overrun. See T-03.

name: accel_supply
source: 21 1B@6 u16/1000 V (5V reference). Should sit rock-solid at 5.0 V ±0.1; a dip = short in the pedal wiring. Verified 5.01 V. MOVED 2026-10-04: the ECU now returns the LONG 21 1B form (0C 61 1B, 10 data bytes) in all 1929 replies since 2026-10-03; @6 reads 0 (spikes to 7.7 = not a voltage) while @8 sits at 4.94-5.02 V (median 4.978) through engine-off, idle and revs = the 5 V reference. The old @6 value (5.01 V, 2026-08) came from the short 12-byte form. Re-read through the decoder after a restart 2026-10-04 (engine idling): 4.98 V, status ok -> proven.
label: Pedal supply
description: 5 V reference — rock-solid 5.0 V ±0.1.
